examples.question_text:
a. A fair coin is flipped $80$ times. How many heads would you expect?
b. A fair six-sided die is rolled $180$ times. How many $2$s would you expect?
examples.solution_text:
a. Heads has probability $\frac{1}{2}$.
$\begin{aligned}f &= np\\&=80\times\frac{1}{2}\\&=40\end{aligned}$
b. Each face has probability $\frac{1}{6}$.
$\begin{aligned}f &= np\\&=180\times\frac{1}{6}\\&=30\end{aligned}$

Two of the $5$ equally likely sectors are blue.
$P(B)=\frac{2}{5}$
$\begin{aligned}f &= np\\&=75\times\frac{2}{5}\\&=30\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
A fair ten-sided die has faces labelled $2$, $2$, $2$, $4$, $5$, $5$, $6$, $7$, $8$, $9$. It is rolled $80$ times.
a. Find the expected frequency of rolling a $2$.
b. Find the expected frequency of rolling an odd number.
examples.solution_text:
a. Three of the $10$ equally likely faces show $2$.
$P(2)=\frac{3}{10}$
$\begin{aligned}f &= np\\&=80\times\frac{3}{10}\\&=24\end{aligned}$
b. The odd faces are $5$, $5$, $7$, $9$: count both faces showing $5$.
$\begin{aligned}P(\text{odd})&=\frac{4}{10}\\&=0.4\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}f &= np\\&=80\times0.4\\&=32\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: The probability that a biased coin lands on heads is $\frac{3}{5}$. It is flipped $70$ times. Find the expected frequency of heads.
A fair ten-sided die numbered from $1$ to $10$ is rolled $250$ times. Find the expected frequency of rolling a $13$.
A fair spinner has $8$ equal sectors, exactly $1$ of which is yellow. It is spun $60$ times. Find the exact expected frequency of yellow as a decimal.
examples.solution_text:
$P(\text{yellow})=\frac{1}{8}$
$\begin{aligned}f &= np\\&=60\times\frac{1}{8}\\&=7.5\end{aligned}$
An actual count is a whole number, but an expected frequency can be a decimal.

examples.question_text: A game has only two outcomes: win or lose. The probability of winning is $0.35$. If you play $120$ games, how many losses would you expect?
examples.solution_text:
Winning and losing are complementary events.
$\begin{aligned}P(\text{lose})&=1-0.35\\&=0.65\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}f &= np\\&=120\times0.65\\&=78\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: A fair coin gives P(heads)=1/2, so 80×1/2=40 heads. A fair six-sided die gives P(2)=1/6, so 180×1/6=30 twos.
The TikZ radii divide the circle into five equal 72-degree sectors. Two labels are B, matching the prompt. P(B)=2/5 and 75×2/5=30.
There are ten equally likely faces, including three labelled 2: 80×3/10=24. The four odd faces are 5, 5, 7 and 9: P(odd)=4/10=0.4 and 80×0.4=32.
Use the supplied biased-coin probability: f=70×3/5=42 heads.
The available faces are 1 through 10, so P(13)=0. The expected frequency is 250×0=0.
One of eight equal sectors is yellow, so P(yellow)=1/8. The exact expected frequency is 60/8=7.5; it need not be an integer.
Win and lose exhaust the outcomes and are mutually exclusive. P(lose)=1−0.35=0.65, giving 120×0.65=78 expected losses.
